messages.subject: computations on 3D variable
parts:
Hi nimble community, 

I'm interested in computing a derived variable from a model parameter with three dimensions. However, I get an error when compiling (toy example below), and from perusing this thread, it seems like computations on variables with >2 dimensions is not supported. I'm working to reformat my data and code to try to accomplish what I need to do with a 2D variable, but in the meantime I'm curious if anyone has encountered the same issue and found workarounds.

Thanks!

Neil 

library(nimble)

code <- nimble::nimbleCode({
  for( i in 1 : 100 ) {
    for( j in 1 : 10 ) {
      for( k in 1 : 5 ) {
        x[i, j, k] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 1)
      }
    }
  }
  mean_x <- mean(x[1:100, 1:10, 1:5])
})

out <- nimbleMCMC(
  code = code,
  thin = 1,
  inits = list(x = array(rnorm( 100 * 10 * 5, 0, 1), dim = c(100, 10, 5))),
  nburnin = 100,
  niter = 200,
  nchains = 1)

Error in eigenizeNameStrided(code, symTab, typeEnv, workEnv) :
  Error, cannot eigenize a map of dimensions > 2
Error: There is some problem at the Eigen processing step for this code:
 {
    model$mean_x[1] <<- mean(model$x[1:100, 1:10, 1:5])
----------------

messages.subject: Re: computations on 3D variable
parts:
Hi Neil,

The best solution would be to write a nimbleFunction that computes the mean of a 3D variable using for-loops.  Actually you just need one for loop, as the other two dimensions can be handled at a 2D object.

Perry
